prompt: A carpenter checks corners by measuring three sides. Which set of side lengths makes a **right** triangle?
hint: A triangle is right exactly when the squares of its two shorter sides add up to the square of its longest side. Test each set that way.

hints.text: A triangle is right exactly when the squares of its two shorter sides add up to the square of its longest side. Test each set that way.
Check the set $9$, $12$, $15$: compare $9^2 + 12^2$ with $15^2$ and see whether the two values match.
$81 + 144 = 225 = 15^2$, so the sides $9$, $12$, $15$ make a right triangle, which is choice B.

explanation: The converse of the Pythagorean Theorem says a triangle is right exactly when the squares of the two shorter sides add to the square of the longest.
For choice B, $9^2 + 12^2 = 81 + 144 = 225$, and $15^2 = 225$ as well, so this set works.

The other sets fail the test, since $36 + 49 = 85 
eq 64$, $16 + 25 = 41 
eq 36$ and $25 + 36 = 61 
eq 100$, so the answer is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Carpenters really do this
steps: Builders square up a foundation by measuring $3$ ft along one edge, $4$ ft along the other, and checking that the diagonal is exactly $5$ ft.
Any multiple works, so $9$-$12$-$15$ is the same trick at triple size — handy when the corner is big.
